problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (\frac{1}{2}F)$ for the vector field $F$ where

$$
F=x{e}^{2x}\,i-y{e}^{2x}\,j+x{z}^{2}\,k.
$$

feedback.problem:
Calculate $∇\cdot (F-2G)$ for the vector fields $F$ and $G,$ where

$$
F={x}^{2}y\,i+{y}^{2}\,j,\,∇\cdot G=xy+{y}^{2}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F$ and $G$ are vector fields and $k$ is a constant, then we have the following  linearity properties for divergence:

- $∇\cdot (kF)=k∇\cdot F$

- $∇\cdot (F+G)=∇\cdot F+∇\cdot G.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F-2G) & =∇\cdot F-∇\cdot (2G) \\  & =∇\cdot F-2∇\cdot G.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to calculate $∇\cdot F.$ In doing so, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}) \\  & =2xy+2y.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the linearity properties, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\cdot (F-2G) & =∇\cdot F-2∇\cdot G \\  & =2xy+2y-2\cdot (xy+{y}^{2}) \\  & =2xy+2y-2xy-2{y}^{2} \\  & =2y-2{y}^{2} \\  & =2y(1-y).\end{aligned}
$$
